reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows FSP as a pre-weld treatment to improve fusion welding, not as a standalone repair method. It does not provide evidence for FSP repair of nickel-based superalloys, nor does it demonstrate improved high-temperature mechanical performance under aggressive service conditions. The hypothesis overstates the support by extrapolating from pre-weld treatment to repair without direct evidence.
premises: FSP can be applied as a repair technique (not just pre-weld treatment) on nickel-based superalloys to eliminate hot cracking.
FSP operates below the melting point, avoiding liquid film formation and microsegregation.
FSP induces dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement in the processed zone.
The refined, homogenized microstructure directly translates to improved high-temperature mechanical performance under aggressive conditions.
The cited evidence on FSP pre-weld treatment for aluminum and nickel alloys directly supports its use as a standalone repair method.
